_comment: Hand-authored. The transition dispatcher $EB18: game start, room change, warp-style exits, special screens, corridor load and the stage end, bank 7 $EB08-$ED07 (inline far-call arguments and the TGL order table are claimed elsewhere). The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: Place the ship at the start position
regions.description: Slot 0's x := $78, y := $90 and its facing $0668 := 4 (down). Called by the game start ($EB37) and after a corridor in a TGL-less game ($ECF0). RUN: (120, 144), facing 4.

regions.name: THE TRANSITION DISPATCHER: new game, or the ship is already playing
regions.description: Entered by JMP from the stage step ($E663) when $A0 bit 0 is set (a room exit or a finished stage), and at the very start of a game. Slot 0's type $0500 = 0 means there is no ship yet: this is the START OF A GAME ($EB1D); anything else is a transition during play ($EB78). This routine does not return until the new room or corridor is up and begun ($ED1D); the loop is suspended meanwhile (see the room-change scrolls).

regions.name: Game start: HUD labels and the move history
regions.description: $E15F draws the HUD labels. If the start mode $2F is below 3 (0 new game, 1 password, 2 CONTINUE) the ten-byte move history $04F0-$04F9 is filled with 4 ('no move yet'); mode 3 (the progress recorder) keeps it. RUN: modes 0 and 2 gave all 4, mode 3 kept $77.

regions.name: Game start: reset the mode, ship, and find the room
regions.description: $2F := 0, bank 5, the ship placed ($EB08), exit code $A4 := 4, bank 5 $802D (find the map record of ($52, $53) -> $E4). Then $30 bit 5 (a labyrinth special-screen game: CONTINUE or a password restores one) goes to $EB60, otherwise the corridor start below.

regions.name: Game start: corridor 0 (or a random corridor in the demo)
regions.description: $50 := 0, $51 := 0 (corridor 0, the opening stage), $77 := 0 (the TGL order index). In a demo ($30 bit 7) $51 := a random value AND $0F (corridors 0-15). $D4F3 switches the NMI on and it jumps to the corridor loader $EC94. RUN: $51 = 0 in a normal start, 5 in a demo run (random).

regions.name: Game start with a saved labyrinth position (CONTINUE / password)
regions.description: A TGL game has no labyrinth and goes to the corridor start ($EB5A). Otherwise it loads the labyrinth ship's sprite sheet and the weapon sprites ($F6F5, $F717) and looks at the map record at $E4 (the player's position): byte 0 bit 7 (a special screen) -> $EC23, an ordinary room -> $EC76. RUN, CONTINUE with $2F = 2: place ship, 802D, F6F5, F717, EEE0 ... fade in, begin play at frame 83; TGL: the corridor loader at once.

regions.name: A transition during play: the move history
regions.description: $A4 is the exit that was taken (0 N, 2 W, 6 E, 8 S, 4 = into a corridor). Unless it is 4 the ten-byte history $04F0-$04F9 is shifted up one place and $A4 stored at $04F0 (the newest). The history feeds the seal puzzle (seven alternating moves) and the loop gates. RUN: exit 0 gave [0, 4, 4 ...], exit 6 [6, 4, 4 ...].

regions.name: Which kind of exit? ($A0 bit 1)
regions.description: $A0 bit 1 set goes to the warp-style exit at $EBD4; clear is an ordinary room change. The bit is set (with bit 0) by two places found by scanning for ORA #$03 / STA $A0: bank 3 $9009 (the ship on a warp panel with the right key, sound $3B) and bank 1 $8057 (the gate's ship being pushed up). CORRECTION: ram.json called it 'the player died'; the death goes through bank 6 $8239 to GAME OVER instead.

regions.name: Transition: forget the open box, clear the objects, corridor or labyrinth?
regions.description: $56 := $FF (no pick-up box is open), every object but the ship removed ($EA68), bank 5. $30 bit 6 clear (the labyrinth) -> $EBA5. In a corridor: not a demo -> the stage end at $EBFE; in a demo JMP $FF4A (the demo is over, the game restarts).

regions.name: Room change: after a miniboss, restore the room music
regions.description: If the boss phase $70 is set (a miniboss was just beaten) it plays sound $1F and then the labyrinth music of the area, $EF16[$50] (the area table), and clears $70.

regions.name: Room change: load the next room and begin
regions.description: The order, RUN: bank 5 $802D (find the record of the new position), $8015 (read it: the position $52/$53 moves one cell), $8003 (build the room buffer), $8030, $F09A (the scroll, which ends by calling $8006 for the cell classes), $ED44 (the key-door pictures), $8039, then A = 0 and JMP $ED1D (begin play, no jingle). RUN: the north exit took 81 frames in all, the east exit 98; ($52, $53) went (8, 12) -> (8, 11) and (9, 12).

regions.name: Warp-style exit: flash the ship
regions.description: If the exit is not 4 (into a corridor) slot 0's $0578 is set to bit 7 on, bit 6 off, its $0788 := $80 and 60 game-loop passes run ($FF8B, Y = $3C): the ship's leaving animation. Exit code 4 skips it. RUN: 59 frames to $EBEE.

regions.name: Warp-style exit: remove the ship and the objects
regions.description: Slot 0 := type 0, 20 more passes, every object removed, bank 5. RUN: $EBFE at frame 79 (60 + 20); with exit code 4 at frame 19.

regions.name: Where to? Read the target record
regions.description: $70 := 0; X = $A4; $18/$19 := the map record of the neighbour in that direction (the pointer table at $E0: N $E0, W $E2, own room $E4, E $E6, S $E8). If $30 has bit 5 or 6 set (a special screen or a corridor) it goes to $EC54, otherwise to the next block.

regions.name: Go to a SPECIAL SCREEN (fade, sound, load)
regions.description: $EDD1 fade out, sound $1F, $D4E3 (NMI off), $F269 (not read), bank 5 $802D. RUN: the fade took 8 frames, sound $1F at frame 87, EE1D at 87.

regions.name: Special screen: draw it and the key-door pictures
regions.description: JSR $EE1D (loads the screen type $51 and its scene, see the labyrinth notes) and $ED44. Also reached by JMP from $EB75 and $ECF3.

regions.name: Special screen: clear the ship, set sprite 0
regions.description: Slot 0 := type 0, $36 := 0, sprite 0's y $BF ($D51E), then a far call to bank 6 $8000 (one object-loop pass; the three inline bytes at $EC38).

regions.name: Special screen: fade in, and the gate-cleared ship entrance
regions.description: Scroll zeroed ($D4FD), fade in ($ED98). Screen type $51 = 5 (a corridor gate whose corridor is cleared) goes to $EC4C; anything else begins play with A = $80, i.e. WITH the jingle ($ED1D).

regions.name: Cleared gate: the scripted ship entrance
regions.description: JSR $F4B7 (the type-$81 ship entrance, see the stage-clear notes), then begin play with A = 0 (no jingle).

regions.name: Special screen or corridor?
regions.description: $30 AND $60 = $20 (a labyrinth special screen) -> $EC5B; otherwise (bit 6: a corridor) JMP $ECBD, the stage end.

regions.name: Leaving a special screen: into a corridor, another special screen, or a room
regions.description: Exit code 4 (the gate) -> $EC8C. Otherwise the neighbour's record: byte 0 bit 7 set (another special screen) -> $EC12, else an ordinary room -> $EC65. RUN: exit W with a special record went through EC12 and EE1D, with an ordinary one through EC65 and EEE0.

regions.name: Leaving to an ordinary room: fade, load, fade in
regions.description: $EDD1 fade out, sound $1F, NMI off, $F269, bank 5 $802D, $EEE0 (read the area, load the scene, build and draw the room), $ED44, scroll zeroed, sprite 0, $ED98 fade in, begin play with A = $80 (the jingle). RUN: $EEE0 at frame 87, begin play at 110 with sound $3C.

regions.name: Into a corridor from its gate
regions.description: The corridor number = byte 2 of the gate's map record ($18),2 AND $7F -> $51. RUN: the record of corridor 5's entrance ($8C09) gave $51 = 5 after 19 frames (the 20-pass wait of $EBEE).

regions.name: CORRIDOR LOAD: start corridor $51
regions.description: Entered from the gate, the game start, and the end of each corridor. Sound $1F (the pre-corridor jingle), the corridor launch $F282 (fade, the take-off flight), $EF6C (the corridor's scene and stream), the ship at (128, 160) ($0530/$0518), sprite 0, the fade in ($ED98), the corridor's music $EF2A[$51], then begin play with A = 0. Bank 5 must be live on entry (the launch calls bank 5 $8000).

regions.name: STAGE END: which corridor was it?
regions.description: Reached by JMP from $EC58. $51 = 0 -> $ECE7; 1-20 -> $ECE4 (mark it cleared first); 21 -> $ECC7; 22 -> $ECE1.

regions.name: Corridor 21: the clear, then the planet cutscene
regions.description: $F506 (stage clear), then a far call to bank 0 $8012 (the starfield, $88F5; inline bytes at $ECCD).

regions.name: Corridor 21: reload the ship's sprites
regions.description: $F6E5 and $F717.

regions.name: Corridor 21: the planet scene
regions.description: Far call to bank 2 $801B ($8836: the planet scene; the three inline bytes at $ECD9).

regions.name: Corridor 21: on to corridor 22
regions.description: $51 += 1 (22) and JMP $EC94: the last corridor loads. See the ending notes.

regions.name: Corridor 22: the clear (never returns)
regions.description: $F506 runs the final score screen and the ending; it does not return.

regions.name: Corridors 1-20: mark cleared
regions.description: $EFBA marks the corridor cleared (the flags the map reads, $04A9/$04AA; read, not run).

regions.name: Corridors 0-20: the clear; then labyrinth or TGL?
regions.description: $F506 (stage clear, key, the landing flight), then $30 bit 1 set (a TGL game) goes to $ECF6, otherwise back to the labyrinth.

regions.name: Back to the labyrinth
regions.description: The ship placed ($EB08) and the special screen / room at the player's position drawn ($EC23).

regions.name: TGL: the item screen
regions.description: Far call to bank 3 $8018 (YOU GOT ITEM, the reward screen; inline bytes at $ECF9).

regions.name: TGL: the next corridor
